findings.title: D5's per-figure containment of a malformed pin has no test: removing either twin-scan guard leaves test_sources.py ALL PASS
findings.scenario: The twin scan in _resolve_pin (sources.py:240-243) walks EVERY artworkPins entry for every pinned figure. Only the two guards `isinstance(e, dict)` (:241) and `isinstance(e.get('file'), str)` (:242) stop one bad sibling entry from crashing the others. Take a table {"CNX_A": <valid alias>, "_note": "a comment someone left in the table"}, or a second pin with file: 5. With either guard removed, resolving CNX_A raises AttributeError or TypeError, so every batch that holds any pinned figure fails, `sources.py --json` exits 1, and figure-run aborts the chapter. D5 says "a malformed pin is a typo, not a run-wide fault", and D11 asks for every D2–D6 rule with a control plus a mutation pass over the resolver. The current code is CORRECT: CNX_A resolves, and the bad entry is either pin-invalid on its own or ignored. The gap is the test. Every malformed-shape test (test_sources.py:467-482) uses a one-entry table, so the twin loop never meets a malformed sibling. Mitigation, which may justify down-rating to Minor: the regression would be loud (exit 1, nothing bought), and the JS validator rejects a non-object pin entry before a buy.

findings.title: A pin through a symlink resolves to a file outside its tree, or into our own Translated_IS output
findings.scenario: _pin_invalid (:198-206) checks only the DECLARED `file` parts: no `..`, no Translated_IS segment, and a source suffix. _resolve_pin then accepts any `root / file` for which `path.is_file()` (:249) is true. is_file follows symlinks, and nothing resolves the path or checks that it stays inside the tree. Example: pin {kind: alias, edition: updates-2e, file: 'OSX/link_own.eps'}, where OSX/link_own.eps is a symlink to first-edition/Ch_19/Translated_IS/CNX_Own_IS.eps. The figure resolves as a hit with via: alias, and a buy would compose our own translated output. The JS validator's `_IS`-stem rule does not catch it, because the declared stem is `link_own`. A directory symlink ('dirlink/Elsewhere.eps') reaches a file outside every configured tree the same way. D5 requires a file that crosses _OWN_OUTPUT_DIRS to be pin-invalid. Realism: low.

findings.title: An artworkPins table that is a string is silently ignored (pins dropped, exit 0); other non-object tables crash the resolver
findings.scenario: Config "artworkPins": "TODO". At :331, `for k in pins` iterates the string's characters, no character folds onto a real basename, and every pinned figure falls through to the normal lookup. findings.scenario: D2 says a key acts by its presence, and that a pin cannot resurrect a retired or superseded figure. retiredFigures honours presence: a null value still refuses, as '(no reason recorded)'. findings.title: The retire's rollback tests cannot detect a partial restore: a version that restores only one of several deleted copies passes them all
findings.scenario: The four retire rollback tests (test lines 198, 216, 229 and 258) all inject the fault on unlink 1 or 2, in a batch of at most two names. So at most ONE translated copy is ever deleted before the fault. A regression in applyRetire's rollback call (tools/retire-translated-figure.js:233) that restores only the first, or only the last, deleted file passes the whole test file. verdicts.measured: Six mutants each leave test_sources.py at ALL PASS: P1 (no backslash rule), P2 (no drive-letter rule), P3 (twins ignore edition), P6 (twins without the dict guard), M13 (`not value` in place of `not value.strip()`) and P5 (a case-sensitive suffix). The kill control, which accepts an unknown kind, crashed the suite. Demos: (a) backslash and 'C:/...' pins are pin-invalid in the real code and pin-missing under P1/P2. (b) The same relative file pinned in two editions resolves both in the real code and refuses both as pin-conflict under P3; the JS validator's control at figure-config-validate.test.js:407 accepts that config. (c) A string entry beside a valid pin: the valid pin resolves in the real code, and under P6 resolve_report and run_cli --json raise AttributeError. P5: an upper-case .EPS pin resolves in the real code and is pin-invalid under P5. Correction to (d): M13 changes behaviour only for reason. Whitespace-only kind, edition and file are still refused as pin-invalid by later rules; only a whitespace-only reason is accepted, and the validator's rule that a reason has over 40 characters catches that in CI. Every case fails closed or loudly.
